description:
🚀 We are Orbitelle — curious, self-driven builders who enjoy coding and design, turning complex ideas into things people can interact with and learn from. We love combining technical depth with real creativity.

Looking for teammates skilled in coding, UI/UX or graphic design, data visualization, AI/ML, animation, or Earth science/education — but curiosity and reliability matter more than any one skill. Excited about space, STEM, or building cool things under a deadline? Join us! 💙
summary: ASTRA is a browser-based mission simulator that puts children aged 7–12 in command of a lunar outpost near the Moon's South Pole. Instead of a quiz or a static dashboard, players make real engineering trade-offs: every decision about power, water, oxygen, food, and radiation shielding costs something elsewhere. A deterministic Python simulation engine computes every consequence from a seed and a decision history, so missions are fully reproducible and can be replayed and investigated after failure. A Mission Ladder of four difficulty levels, a "What If? Lab" for safe experimentation, and investigation reports that explain why a mission failed turn abstract space-engineering concepts into lived experience. The NASA Reality Hub connects real DONKI space-weather data, ISS radiation history, and OSDR biology research to the game, with every value honestly labeled LIVE, CACHED, ARCHIVED, or SIMULATED so children never mistake a fictional training scenario for an actual NASA measurement. ASTRA addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by teaching that survival in space is a continuous balancing act, not a single right answer.
details:
ASTRA simulates a 20-day lunar South Pole mission. Each day presents an event (reduced sunlight, a solar storm warning, equipment malfunction, research opportunity) with 2–3 decision options, each carrying real benefits and real costs across interconnected systems: power, oxygen, water, food, shielding, and crew health. A FastAPI backend with a pure-Python deterministic simulation engine owns all game-state math; the React + Vite frontend only ever displays what the backend returns, so results are never faked client-side. Missions store only their seed and decision history, then replay them to reconstruct state — making every run reproducible and fully auditable, including for a "Mission Investigation Report" that explains the root cause of a failed mission.

The NASA Reality Hub integrates live NASA DONKI space-weather events, real ISS radiation-dose history, and curated OSDR space-biology studies, each tagged with a LIVE/CACHED/ARCHIVED/SIMULATED status so real observations are never confused with fictional training scenarios. A "What If? Lab" lets players experiment with parameters on an isolated copy of the simulation without touching their real mission. A Mission Ladder (First Landing → Storm Season → The Long Night → Commander) unlocks progressively harder configurations. 166 automated backend tests cover the simulation formulas, decision validation, and deterministic replay.

Tools/languages: Python (FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, pytest), JavaScript/React (Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Recharts, Lucide icons), SQLite, deployed on Render (backend) and Vercel (frontend).

Creativity/impact: rather than teaching space science through text or trivia, ASTRA makes the player feel the engineering trade-offs NASA engineers actually face — there is no "correct" choice, only costs — while keeping every real NASA data point clearly separated from game fiction.
dataRefs: NASA Artemis — Lunar South Pole Exploration
